src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/init.py

Python · Tier A

Export the verified-procedure cache API without performing lookup or replay.

Responsibilities

  • Expose plan/step contracts and the RAM-or-standalone-SQL cache facade used by native integration.

Boundaries

  • This package stores executable procedures; it does not cache answers, inference or authority grants.

Lifecycle

  • Import exports model and storage types; runtime.py decides when lookup and capture are eligible.

State

  • Importing this facade does not open the cache database.

Security

  • Consumers must revalidate loaded procedures against current capability and execution scope.

Collaborators

  • models.py defines bounded contracts; store.py owns retention and exact-prompt associations.

Public surface

  • VerifiedExecutionCache, VerifiedExecutionPlan and VerifiedExecutionStep are the package exports.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/context.py

Python · Tier A

Bind reusable procedures to authoritative Gateway, directory and resource identity.

Responsibilities

  • Derive effective execution scope and compare shell working directories with verified Git resources.

Boundaries

  • Never discover targets, inspect live repositories, or infer a resource from branch/output history.

Lifecycle

  • Capture snapshots relevant roots; lookup and direct proposal compare them with current configuration.

State

  • Reads conversation authority and working context; returns detached scope/resource descriptions.

Security

  • Remove credential/session grants from identity and reject unresolved or ambiguous execution roots.

Collaborators

  • execution/paths.py resolves target-platform paths; conversation_working_context.py normalizes resource facts.

Public surface

  • scope_for, mismatch, resources_for and validate_resources define scope matching and bounded reasons.

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/direct.py

Python · Tier A

Propose one verified read through ordinary native operation acceptance.

Responsibilities

  • Revalidate an exact single-step recipe and construct a normal tool-call message for eligible fresh tasks.

Boundaries

  • Does not execute a tool, reserve inference or claim an operation; native acceptance owns those transitions.

Lifecycle

  • proposal performs one check; accepted marks pending inside the acceptance transaction; after_result records the outcome.

State

  • Mutates bounded execution_cache diagnostics and direct-attempt markers; loads and revalidates the current cache row.

Security

  • Only shell.command and python.transform qualify, with current safety/authorization, no grants, bindings or transient handles.

Collaborators

  • runtime.py owns load validation; execution/authorization.py checks permission; focus.py releases stale presentation.

Public surface

  • proposal returns a native call or None; direct_ineligibility, accepted and after_result define the narrow shortcut.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/extraction.py

Python · Tier A

Prove a minimal reusable read graph from accepted terminal evidence.

Responsibilities

  • Walk backward from accepted evidence, verify fresh receipts and convert proven dependencies into symbolic steps.

Boundaries

  • Discovery alone is not execution evidence; writes, unknown effects, background jobs and self-assertions cannot seed plans.

Lifecycle

  • Whole-task capture requires accepted completion; explicit step retention narrows the evidence root without changing receipts.

State

  • Copies arguments and reads ordered receipts; emits a bounded plan without executing it or storing outputs.

Security

  • Reject stale evidence, copied data, lossy redaction markers and unproven historical handles before plan admission. Credential-looking literal values are not independently filtered.

Collaborators

  • safety.py enforces effects and argument contracts; native/evidence.py checks staleness; models.py validates graph shape.

Public surface

  • extract_plan builds a whole-task recipe; extract_step proves one independent read; successful classifies receipts.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
successful 56 Require an executed, complete success or completed process observation receipt.
extract_plan 66 Build a bounded backward dependency graph from accepted evidence, or raise a bounded Discard reason. Every executed effect must be explained as a read; arguments and bindings are copied, not receipts.
extract_step 316 An independently reusable completed read, even within a mixed-action task. The normal extractor supplies the same contract/effect/dependency proof. Only its terminal selection is narrowed; original receipts are never modified.

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/focus.py

Python · Tier A

Advance transient cache focus only after matching fresh successful read receipts.

Responsibilities

  • Project the next verified tool, compare calls with symbolic bindings and release focus when execution diverges.

Boundaries

  • Focus narrows model presentation but never authorizes execution or declares the current task complete.

Lifecycle

  • Before-call checks exact arguments; after-call advances once per durable receipt; completion corrections may retain focus.

State

  • Mutates verified_fast_path and recipe fields in conversation state; reads fresh receipt IDs from RunStore.

Security

  • Credential/approval waits pause the cursor; failed or mismatched reads release it; historical results are never reused.

Collaborators

  • runtime.py emits cache events; extraction.py classifies success; json_pointer.py resolves fresh bindings.

Public surface

  • decision_tools, before_call, after_call and release integrate focus with the native decision lifecycle.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/identity.py

Python · Tier A

Hash exact prompt, execution scope and structural capability contracts.

Responsibilities

  • Build cache keys from canonical prompts and effective scope; fingerprint schemas and effect class.

Boundaries

  • Credential grants, approval mode and live session handles are not reusable procedure identity.

Lifecycle

  • Lookup recomputes prompt/scope identity; validation compares each stored capability fingerprint.

State

  • Pure hashing creates no files and retains no prompt text outside the returned digest values.

Security

  • Strip descriptive schema metadata only at schema positions; defaults, enums and constants remain data.

Collaborators

  • prompt_identity.py canonicalizes wording; native/history.py selects scope; models.py hashes JSON.

Public surface

  • cache_identity returns key/prompt/scope digests; contract_hash identifies executable schema semantics.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/management.py

Python · Tier A

Manage retained cache procedures from durable receipts without executing them.

Responsibilities

  • Inspect eligible completed reads, pin verified steps or exact prompts, list retained recipes and remove them.

Boundaries

  • Management never asks a model, executes tools, discovers remote targets or assembles a plan from arbitrary UI input.

Lifecycle

  • Reconstruct execution from RunStore, repeat extraction and scope checks, then change retention through the current RAM or standalone SQL cache owner.

State

  • Reads native runs/receipts and writes cache recipes/aliases; paginated conversation inspection deduplicates recipes.

Security

  • Reject mismatched conversations, unresolved interaction context and invalid plans. Show saved prompt text only after identity proof; unassigned entries do not reconstruct old prompts.

Collaborators

  • extraction.py proves receipt-owned plans; context.py binds resources; store.py owns atomic retention; API callers own access checks.

Public surface

  • FastCacheManagement exposes prompt/step eligibility, pinning, paginated listings and recipe removal.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/memory_store.py

Python · Tier A

Own the running Controller execution cache through indexed RAM recipe and exact-prompt records. CacheRecords maintains wire projections and ordered retention indexes in the same transaction as writes. MemoryExecutionCache coalesces equivalent recipes, protects explicit prompt pins and applies bounded LRU retention only to learned entries; checkpoints persist authoritative rows. It returns detached data and rejects runtime SQL access. Extraction, current policy and fresh execution receipts remain separate requirements for reuse.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
schemas 30 Build typed recipe/alias schemas from the shared compatibility SQL catalog at bootstrap. Both tables use cache_key identity; prompt/recipe indexes support exact lookup, and declared JSON columns become detached structured RAM values.
CacheRecords 49 Maintain transactional derived indexes and bounded wire projections alongside authoritative cache rows. The projections preserve the existing JSON-string facade while avoiding whole-cache re- encoding on reads; all changes publish with the owning record transaction.
CacheRecords.changed 54 Re-encode only changed JSON fields in one public row projection, delete that projection with its record, and maintain ordered recipe listing/LRU indexes. Pinned recipes enter the display index but are absent from unpinned eviction order. A hook failure rolls back the row and derived changes together.
MemoryExecutionCache 108 Serve the Controller cache through indexed RAM records and checkpoint persistence. Keep shared procedure recipes separate from exact-prompt aliases, preserve independently pinned triggers and bound only learned recipes. Loading/updating storage does not prove current execution permission or freshness.
MemoryExecutionCache.connect 129 Reject compatibility SQL access when this facade is backed by the Controller RAM authority. Callers must use typed repository methods or explicit lifecycle-owned recovery/export.
MemoryExecutionCache.get 144 Return a detached bounded-wire recipe projection, overriding prompt identity and output intent from the matching alias. Lookups do not count a hit or execute a cached procedure.
MemoryExecutionCache.delete 167 Resolve an alias to its recipe and optionally require the current plan hash. With an invalidation reason, pinned recipes remain visible with stale_reason; otherwise remove the recipe and all aliases atomically.
MemoryExecutionCache.record_hit 184 Increment recipe and matching alias hit counters only when the current plan hash still matches. Capture one timestamp outside the retryable transaction; concurrent replacement cannot credit a different plan.
MemoryExecutionCache.upsert 206 Detach and validate the bounded plan, derive a shared recipe identity from scope/steps/resources, and atomically update its exact-prompt association, statistics and retention. Learning cannot retarget a user-pinned trigger unless explicitly pinned again. Preserve an existing recipe baseline/source retention, avoid double-counting the same execution, and evict only excess unpinned LRU recipes. Return captured, replaced, success or unchanged without claiming that a tool ran here.
MemoryExecutionCache.entries 349 List detached recipe projections in reverse display order: pinned entries first, then pin/update/identity order. This is management metadata, not a new validation or permission decision.
MemoryExecutionCache.aliases 359 List detached exact-prompt associations with pinned triggers first and deterministic key ordering within equal pin priority. Prompt retention is independent of the shared procedure recipe.
MemoryExecutionCache.remove_prompt 368 Remove only one exact trigger, recompute shared recipe pin time from remaining aliases, and delete the recipe only when no aliases remain. Other prompts sharing the recipe keep their mappings.
MemoryExecutionCache.clear_learned 387 Delete every unpinned recipe and its aliases in one transaction and return the removed recipe count. Explicitly pinned recipes remain outside this learned-entry index.
MemoryExecutionCache.candidates 399 Use exact prompt-hash indexes across recipes/aliases to return at most 256 existing recipes in deterministic identity order. Other scopes support miss diagnostics; this does not perform semantic matching or authorize cross-scope reuse.

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/models.py

Python · Tier A

Constrain reusable read procedures to bounded, ordered steps and fresh bindings.

Responsibilities

  • Validate version, supported capabilities, contiguous step IDs and backward-only dependency bindings.

Boundaries

  • These schemas cannot establish execution success or current permission; extraction and safety do that.

Lifecycle

  • Extraction constructs a plan; loading reparses its canonical JSON before projection or execution.

State

  • Frozen model attributes contain mutable nested mappings, so validation callers detach through JSON.

Security

  • Reject extra fields, invalid connection dependencies and oversize plans/hints instead of truncating.

Collaborators

  • extraction.py proves receipt provenance; safety.py checks contracts, effects and credential absence.

Public surface

  • StepBinding, VerifiedExecutionStep, VerifiedExecutionPlan, Discard, canonical_json and digest.

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/performance.py

Python · Tier A

Compare bounded cache timing baselines without retaining trace payloads.

Responsibilities

  • Validate numeric metrics, pair native timing events and derive conservative presentation fields.

Boundaries

  • Missing/truncated timings cannot establish speedup; invalid optional metadata does not invalidate a verified plan.

Lifecycle

  • Capture measures an execution; reuse compares its metrics; chat persistence keeps only whitelisted presentation.

State

  • Pure transformations read event counters and return bounded models/dictionaries; time is sampled only when requested implicitly.

Security

  • Never store raw event payloads, prompts or arguments in baseline metrics; reject nonfinite/oversize values.

Collaborators

  • runtime.py captures and compares metrics; store.py retains the original baseline; chat consumes presentation.

Public surface

  • ExecutionCacheBaselineV1, baseline, measure, compare, presentation, saved_presentation and direct_metrics.

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py

Python · Tier A

Integrate optional verified-procedure lookup and capture into the native loop.

Responsibilities

  • Check eligibility, load exact-scope plans, project transient hints and capture proven terminal procedures.

Boundaries

  • Ordinary cache failures fall back to native execution; unsupported store schema versions propagate. This optimization does not own authority or durable receipts.

Lifecycle

  • Lookup runs once for a fresh execution; refresh releases stale focus; terminal capture records one outcome and saves state.

State

  • Uses the cache facade beside RunStore: owned Controller paths resolve to RAM/checkpoints; standalone paths use SQLite. Conversation state holds bounded focus/capture fields.

Security

  • Recheck intact literals, capabilities and resources before projection. The legacy secret helper rejects lossy markers only; diagnostics emit reasons rather than raw arguments.

Collaborators

  • store.py persists recipes; extraction.py proves them; focus.py advances fresh results; native/loop.py owns execution.

Public surface

  • lookup, capture, refresh_hint, public_hint and discovery_guard are native integration points; focus observes current dispatch receipts.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/store.py

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/safety.py

Python · Tier A

Reject unsafe, lossy or stale reusable procedure arguments.

Responsibilities

  • Check lossy markers, transient references, read effects, capability schemas and current availability.

Boundaries

  • Rejection is conservative and cannot prove arbitrary code harmless; existing effect classification owns that decision.

Lifecycle

  • Capture and load both validate plans before retaining or projecting them; invalid plans raise Discard.

State

  • Validation copies argument mappings and reparses plan JSON; no operation is executed or store opened.

Security

  • Preserve literal values; secret_check rejects [redacted] markers only and ignores its legacy secrets argument. Reject copied historical results without fresh bindings.

Collaborators

  • identity.py supplies schema fingerprints; native/progress.py supplies effects; extraction.py supplies proven bindings.

Public surface

  • validate_plan, read_only, argument_safety, secret_check, strings and copied_result support cache admission.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation

secret_check 73 Keep the legacy call signature while rejecting only the case-sensitive [redacted] marker. The secrets argument is unused: current validation does not scan known credential values, encodings or literal-looking secrets. Procedures retain exact admitted arguments; effect/schema/dependency checks remain separate.
argument_safety 80 Reject transient dependencies and optionally lossy markers before retaining a procedure.

src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/store.py

Python · Tier A

Select the Controller RAM cache or standalone SQLite recipe/alias storage.

Responsibilities

  • Coalesce compatible recipes, maintain prompt aliases, record hits and retain explicitly pinned procedures.

Boundaries

  • Hub-owned paths return MemoryExecutionCache. Standalone SQL storage does not prove effects or permissions; callers validate before insertion and after loading.

Lifecycle

  • The facade reuses the existing hub repository; standalone connections validate the baseline. Both implementations atomically coalesce rows and bound unpinned retention.

State

  • The Controller owns indexed RAM records and checkpoint durability. The standalone SQL implementation creates new files with mode 0600 and closes scoped connections.

Security

  • Use bound SQL values and plan hashes for guarded updates; invalid pinned recipes retain a stale reason for management.

Collaborators

  • models.py serializes bounded plans; performance.py validates optional baselines; runtime.py handles failure fallback.

Public surface

  • VerifiedExecutionCache supports lookup, capture, retention and counters; recipe_identity excludes per-prompt output intent.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/28-execution-cache.md

@see src/agent_runtime/execution_cache/runtime.py
